analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only, so no executable security regression appears in the supplied evidence.

docs/architecture/inference.md: the supplied units (head lines 1648-2275) fall outside the changed ranges (head 404-413 and 1053-1073). They contain only unchanged MiMo, Qwen4 and Flint prose, which is not new behavior. The changed hunks are visible only through a truncated patch excerpt:
- Load-gate eviction and pre-accept now release retained free KV segments and drop the MLX buffer cache first.
- Segmented paged admission parks released 64 MiB segments per pool (up to min(2 GiB, grant/8)), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. The next admission of the same size class reinstalls them.
- The excerpt cuts off at 'New segments wrap zero-fil...', so the zeroing and reuse semantics are not visible.

docs/provider/cli-reference.md (patch, head lines 1751-1753): adds three DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* environment variables to the daemon-passthrough table: IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, SEGMENT_RETENTION and SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. Their implementations are not supplied.

Unverified contracts for the next pass (T-028, T-041, TB-007, A-001):
- Whether reinstalled parked KV segments are cleared before reuse by another request, and whether the retention path leaks prior-request KV across consumers. That would extend T-028 residual GPU memory exposure and the cross-tenant surface.
- Whether SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS or SEGMENT_RETENTION can disable zeroing.
- Whether parked segments outside the ledger charge allow memory over-commitment or denial of service (T-016, T-029).
- Whether the environment variables are operator-only local knobs, and whether they are excluded from remote or consumer control.

These are not findings, because the zeroing, reuse and accounting code is not in the supplied evidence. The threat model (T-028 and the TB-007 notes) may need updating once the code is reviewed.
